You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Micron Technology (MU) FY2026 Q3 Earnings: Revenue Surges 346% YoY, Gross Margin Hits Record 84.9%, Q4 Guidance Crushes Estimates

TEXT:
Key Takeaways
Micron Technology delivered an explosive FY2026 third fiscal quarter (ending May 31, 2026). Revenue surged approximately 346% year-over-year to $41.46B, while Non-GAAP adjusted EPS reached $25.11 — more than 12 times the year-ago level — both far exceeding Wall Street consensus estimates. Adjusted gross margin hit a record 84.9%, more than double the level from a year ago. Most critically, Micron's Q4 FY2026 guidance came in 15–22% above expectations on both revenue and EPS, decisively refuting near-term concerns about AI memory demand cooling and peak earnings. The stock surged more than 16% in after-hours trading.
Detailed Breakdown
1. Overall Revenue and Earnings Performance
Quarterly Revenue : $41.46B, +346% YoY, beating consensus of ~$35.69B by approximately $5.77B (+16%)
Non-GAAP EPS : $25.11, +1,200%+ YoY, beating consensus of $20.71 by $4.40 (+21.25%)
Adjusted Gross Margin : 84.9%, beating consensus of 81.9% by ~3 percentage points; more than double the ~40% level from a year ago
Adjusted Operating Income : ~$33.68B, implying an adjusted operating margin of approximately 81.2%
Revenue, EPS, and gross margin all set new single-quarter records, and all accelerated sequentially versus Q2 FY2026
2. Data Center and AI Business (Primary Highlight)
Core Data Center Revenue : $11.52B, approximately 7.5× the year-ago level, beating analyst consensus of ~$6.80B by approximately 69% — the single most important beat in the report
Cloud Storage Revenue : $13.77B, approximately 4× year-over-year, beating consensus of ~$10.69B by approximately 29%
Combined data center + cloud storage revenue: $25.29B, representing approximately 61% of total revenue
HBM Revenue : Exceeded $1B for the second consecutive quarter; full-year 2026 HBM capacity is fully committed with long-term supply agreements with key AI customers
AI server demand continues to drive sustained growth in HBM, high-capacity DRAM , and enterprise SSDs
3. Other Segment Performance
DRAM Revenue : More than tripled year-over-year (+300%+)
NAND Flash Revenue : More than doubled year-over-year (+200%+)
Mobile and Client Business : Revenue ~$11.52B, beating consensus of ~$9.73B by approximately 18%, demonstrating that storage pricing power is spreading beyond AI into broader end markets
Traditional end markets (PC, smartphone, gaming) are also seeing tightening supply as advanced capacity is consumed by AI demand
4. Q4 FY2026 Guidance (Key Upside Driver)
Q4 Revenue Guidance : Range $49B–$51B; midpoint $50.00B , approximately +15.6% above pre-guidance consensus of ~$43.24B
Q4 Non-GAAP EPS Guidance : Range $30–$32; midpoint $31.00 , approximately +22.5% above pre-guidance consensus of ~$25.31
Q4 Capital Expenditure Guidance : ~$10B, approximately +12% above consensus of ~$8.9B; incremental investment focused on HBM, advanced DRAM, and advanced packaging capacity
At guidance midpoints, Q4 revenue would grow approximately 20.6% sequentially from Q3's $41.46B, indicating continued acceleration rather than peak earnings
5. AI Memory Supply and Demand Outlook
CEO Sanjay Mehrotra stated: "The AI era is increasing the criticality of memory and storage, and this trend is still in a very early stage"
HBM supply-demand tightness expected to persist through 2027 and beyond ; overall memory supply constraints to gradually improve from 2028 , with no clear visibility on when supply will fully catch up with demand
Surging demand from AI training, inference, and AI agent applications continues to drive structural upward pressure on memory and storage requirements at data centers
6. Market Context and Investor Considerations
The day before earnings, South Korean media reported rival SK Hynix was slowing HBM4 expansion, sending Micron shares down approximately 13% and reigniting AI demand concerns
Micron's results directly refuted those concerns: core data center revenue beat consensus by nearly 70%, providing the clearest data-point rebuttal possible
Post-earnings, shares that had closed down ~0.4% surged more than 16% in after-hours trading; overnight price ~$1,183 (+12.8%)
The stock had already rallied nearly 270% YTD ahead of the print, raising the performance bar exceptionally high — clearing it by this margin underscores the genuine strength of the AI memory upcycle
Core risk remains the inherent cyclicality of the memory industry: as new capacity gradually comes online, the sustainability of current record-high margins and pricing remains the key long-term question
